title: Grateful Dead Live at Red Vest on 1970-06-13
lineage: SBD MR > R > D > CD + AUD low-gen

ai_review.summary: A matrix source with fair‑to‑poor sound quality, but the show dazzles on Easy Wind, New Speedway and Good Lovin' despite a wonky mix.
ai_review.review: The performance is a high‑energy Hawaiian 1970 set that deadheads love for its standout Easy Wind, New Speedway, Good Lovin' jam and a soaring Lovelight, while Phil’s bass work gets particular praise. The recording is a patchwork of muddy audience AUD and crystal‑clear SBD sections, with an uneven mix that buries Jerry at times, adds snare buzz and static, making the listening experience mixed. Still, the musical moments shine enough to keep this show in many fans’ top‑lists.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating across 21 reviews is ~3.2; reviewers are split between high praise for the performance and strong criticism of the recording, yielding a moderate overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audience (AUD) portions described as muddy, static‑filled and awful; later SBD sections are crystal clear. Mix is uneven – Phil and Bob often high, Jerry buried, snare buzz and overall ‘dank’ but inconsistent sound.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A lively Hawaiian‑vacation set from 1970 with strong jams and happy vibes; however, the erratic source switches make the flow feel disjointed for listeners.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Often backgrounded in the mix, though his playing is noted as hot when audible.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass drives Easy Wind hard; highlighted repeatedly by reviewers.
band_member_comments.Bob: Occasionally pushed forward in the mix and leads some jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Guest keyboard appears on New Speedway; keyboards receive positive nods.
band_member_comments.Drums: Described as razor‑sharp yet also tap‑in‑the‑background with snare buzz.
